title: The Harvest of Marrow Creek
premise: Radio host Mirabel Almeida has spent three years fielding late-night calls from listeners who died the week before, telling himself the static and the voices are hoaxes. When his childhood imaginary friend appears on his porch—unchanged after thirty years—he learns Marrow Creek's founding families fed something in the old well, and that his own family's invisibility was a debt being quietly repaid. As the well refills for its centennial harvest, Mirabel must break the family silence and get his estranged sister and nephew out of town before the count is made. He succeeds at saving them by confessing the truth on-air, but the price is that he takes his nephew's place in the count—and the final broadcast comes from below.
about_author: Mirabel Almeida is the pen name of a former small-market radio producer who grew up in rural Pennsylvania coal country, where abandoned mine shafts and dry wells dotted every childhood summer. Their work blends oral-history intimacy with slow-burn folk horror, exploring what families agree never to say out loud.

chapters.title: Dead Air, Live Voices
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. During his 2 a.m. call-in show, a familiar voice requests a song—a listener whose obituary ran six days ago. The emotional beat is denial curdling into dread as Mirabel realizes the calls have never been pranks, and that tonight's caller knew his childhood nickname, one no living person remembers.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Waited
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. His imaginary friend from 1989 stands on the porch, ageless, patient, and politely insistent that it's 'almost time.' Digging through his mother's locked cedar chest, he finds ledgers of names per generation—the count. The beat is vertigo: loyalty to family memory versus the truth that his family were the feeders, not the spared.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with his sister Dana, who fled Marrow Creek years ago. As the well begins refilling after decades dry, townsfolk grow placid and forgetful, and the friend escorts Mirabel down to show him the previous harvests preserved below—including their father. The beat is corrupted power: the founding families chose comfort over truth, and Mirabel sees how easily he could choose it too.

chapters.title: The Count Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Dana POV. On the night the well crests, Mirabel hijacks his own frequency to broadcast the whole truth, breaking the compulsion holding the town numb and giving Dana time to drive her son past the county line. To balance the ledger, he walks to the well himself. The resolution is bittersweet: dawn finds the town remembering everything, the boy safe—and a new voice requesting a song on the midnight show.
